nodes.name: Open the dashboard
nodes.notes: Served by n8n, not Netlify — see the README.

nodes.name: Bookings
nodes.notes: Thirty days back as well as forward: the page needs recent history to show what was cancelled and what has been done, not just what is next.

nodes.name: Invoices
nodes.notes: Filtered by month in code rather than in a Xero where clause — one fewer piece of syntax to get wrong, and the volume is tiny.

nodes.name: Next payout
nodes.notes: What actually lands in Starling, and when. Revenue and cash are not the same number.

nodes.name: Last deploy
nodes.notes: The deploy workflow specifically, not the newest run of anything — otherwise the light reports on whichever job happened to finish last.

nodes.name: Build the page
nodes.notes: Every value is read through a helper that tolerates a missing field, so one misbehaving system leaves a gap on the page instead of a blank screen.

nodes.name: New leads
nodes.notes: Website enquiries arrive here through the Netlify function, as Leads rather than Contacts. A lead is somebody who asked; a contact is somebody who booked.

nodes.name: Customers
nodes.notes: maxSize is small because only the newest few are shown — the count comes from 'total', which EspoCRM returns regardless of how many records are fetched.

nodes.name: Google reviews
nodes.notes: Five candidates, not one. A single result gave Penarth Healthcare Partnership — a doctors' surgery — because 'IT Surgery' in a town full of surgeries is a genuinely ambiguous search. The page picks the candidate actually named IT Surgery and ignores the rest. Biased to Penarth town centre rather than a home address.
